channel.description: Latest articles from Lynn Group Media (hoganstand.com)

item.title: Grace Murphy is the LGFA Player of the Month for October
item.description: Grace Murphy from Cork club Naomh Abán has been honoured with The Croke Park Hotel/LGFA Player of the Month award for October 2025.

item.title: Westmeath warrior Kieran Martin calls it a day
item.description: Westmeath GAA has led the tributes to Kieran Martin after he brought the curtain down on his 16-year inter-county football career.

item.title: Emma Mulhern on the growth of ladies football in London
item.description: Emma Mulhern is still enjoying every minute of her time with London outfit Holloway Gaels.

item.title: Kerry unveil new home jersey for 2026
item.description: Kerry GAA unveiled its new home jersey for the 2026 season on Friday.

item.title: Shields the hero as Clogher triumph over Emyvale to Ulster club JFC glory
item.description: Clogher Éire Óg are Ulster club junior football champions after securing a late 1-12 to 0-14 victory over Emyvale in Roslea this afternoon.

item.title: Tooreen too strong for Meelick Eircourt in Connacht club IHC decider
item.description: Tooreen stormed to their sixth Connacht club intermediate hurling championship title with a 3-21 to 2-12 win against Meelick Eircourt at King & Moffatt Dr Hyde Park this afternoon.

item.title: Easkey battle past Ballinasloe to Connacht club JHC four-in-a-row
item.description: Easkey (Sligo) are Connacht club junior hurling champions for the fourth year in-a-row after edging out Ballinasloe (Galway) by 2-17 to 2-15 at the Connacht GAA Centre of Excellence in Bekan this afternoon.

item.title: Camogie: Wall double steers 'Barr's to first Munster senior title
item.description: A return of 2-4 from Kate Wall including a dramatic late winner proved pivotal as St Finbarr's saw off a determined De La Salle to secure a first AIB Munster Senior Club Camogie Championship title.

item.title: Four-goal Kilcoo see off Erne Gaels for another Ulster club SFC final berth
item.description: Kilcoo cruised into another Ulster club senior football championship final with a 4-12 to 1-10 win over Erne Gaels Belleek at the Box-It Athletic Grounds this afternoon.
